newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary seals Forum sale agreement with ICH.
newsitem.headline: Hungary seals Forum sale agreement with ICH.

text.p: Hungary on Friday sealed an agreement with Japanese-owned Inter-Continental Hotels Corp (ICH) about the sale of four-star hotel Forum Szalloda Rt.

ICH, whom state privatisation agency APV Rt declared winner of Forum's privatisation tender in August, will pay $49.4 million or 190 percent of the face value for the 94.91 percent stake. ICH will invest more than $11 million within three-years to upgrade Forum to five stars, eventually to run under the name of Hotel Inter-Continental Budapest, APV and ICH officials said. @
"In the history of (privatisation agency) APV this is the first significant non-greenfield Japanese investment," APV's General Director Istvan Kocsis told the signing ceremony.
In a separate development, as the ceremony was underway, Hungary's government had announced it had sacked the entire board of APV following illegal payments to a lawyer acting on its behalf.
ICH, one of the largest hotel groups with more than 190 hotels in 69 countries according to a statement by Forum, is 100 percent owned by the Japanese Saison group. @
Forum's sale represents ICH's return to the Hungarian market after four years.

ICH operated one of Budapest's most distinguished downtown hotels for more than 20 years in franchise until the U.S. Marriott Corp bought the hotel for $53 million after a tender in 1992, where Inter-Continental was among the bidders.
Hungary first attempted to sell Forum Szalloda in February 1996, when 15 companies submitted bids, but the tender was declared unsuccessful. @
In the first half of 1996 Forum posted a pre-tax profit of 413 million forints on net sales of over 1.1 billion forints, APV said in a statement.
